title: Quantitative Biology I - Week-by-Week Schedule
text:
Weekly Plan

Week 1 - Introduction and Predator-Prey Dynamics
Module 1 (Ecology): run guided predator-prey simulation and interpret parameter effects.


Week 2 - Competition Between Species
Module 1 (Ecology): compare coexistence and competitive exclusion scenarios.


Week 3 - Stability, Cycles, and Equilibria
Module 1 (Ecology): parameter sweeps and stability interpretation.


Week 4 - Wright-Fisher and Genetic Drift
Module 2 (Evolution): replicate stochastic trajectories across runs.


Week 5 - Selection and Selective Sweeps
Module 2 (Evolution): compare deterministic expectation and stochastic outcomes.


Week 6 - Establishment of Beneficial Mutations
Module 2 (Evolution): estimate establishment probabilities with repeated trials.


Week 7 - Evolution Synthesis Session
Module 2 (Evolution): integrate drift, selection, and uncertainty.


Week 8 - Gene Expression Dynamics
Module 3 (Cell Biology): simulated expression trajectories and sensitivity.


Week 9 - Regulatory Networks
Module 3 (Cell Biology): analyze behavior under feedback changes.


Week 10 - Stochastic Expression and RNA-seq Variability
Module 3 (Cell Biology): interpret variability metrics and count-like data.


Week 11 - Microbiome Data Fundamentals
Module 4 (Microbiomes): inspect abundance tables and identify broad patterns.


Week 12 - Diversity and Community Structure
Module 4 (Microbiomes): compare groups with diversity and distance-based views.


Week 13 - Environmental Gradients and Variation
Module 4 (Microbiomes): connect metadata to community variation.


Week 14 - Final Project and Integration
Module 4 (Microbiomes): submit and present final exploratory analysis.

title: Quantitative Biology I - Student Overview
text:
Quantitative Biology I introduces computational thinking through real biological questions. This course runs in parallel with your first-year R programming course. In programming class, you learn technical coding foundations; here, you learn how those tools are used to understand living systems.
Across the semester, you will work with models and datasets from:

Ecology and Evolution
Cell Biology
Plant and Environmental Biology
Bioinformatics and Microbiome Science

title: Quantitative Biology I - Student Overview
text:
Learning Outcomes
By the end of this course, you should be able to:

Explain how computational models represent biological processes.
Run and interpret simulations in ecology, evolution, and cell biology.
Distinguish deterministic predictions from stochastic outcomes.
Analyze and visualize biological datasets using guided R workflows.
Modify existing R code and Quarto notebooks to test biological hypotheses.
Communicate biological conclusions using plots and quantitative evidence.

title: Quantitative Biology I - Student Overview
text:
Content Overview

Module 1 (Weeks 1-3): Ecology - Population Dynamics

Lotka-Volterra predator-prey dynamics
Competition between species
Stability, equilibria, and oscillations



Module 2 (Weeks 4-7): Evolution - From Determinism to Randomness

Wright-Fisher model and genetic drift
Selection and selective sweeps
Establishment of beneficial mutations
Expected versus realized trajectories



Module 3 (Weeks 8-10): Cell Biology - Molecular Noise and Regulation

Gene expression dynamics
Regulatory network behavior
Stochastic expression and molecular noise
Variability in RNA-seq-like datasets



Module 4 (Weeks 11-14): Microbiomes - Complex Biological Systems

Microbiome fundamentals and abundance tables
Diversity and community structure
Environmental gradients and variation
Guided exploratory data analysis project
